key_points: Sakeena Fiza, a validation engineer at NVIDIA, describes her role as investigating hardware systems to ensure they function correctly before mass production.
She compares the work to solving a mystery, where engineers must find and fix potential failures in complex AI infrastructure.
items.summary: Sakeena Fiza, a validation engineer at NVIDIA, describes her role as investigating hardware systems to ensure they function correctly before mass production. She compares the work to solving a mystery, where engineers must find and fix potential failures in complex AI infrastructure. Fiza highlights the collaborative nature of the job, involving multiple engineering disciplines to bring new systems to life. She notes that validation engineers act as the first customers, testing devices under real-world conditions to catch issues early. Fiza arrived at NVIDIA after studying computer science and engineering at the University of California, Irvine, driven by a fascination with systems design. She expresses excitement about future products in the pipeline that she believes will change the world.
items.title: Sakeena Fiza Explains NVIDIA Validation Engineering Role

key_points: The article argues that current AI auditing methods fail to capture broad societal risks because they lack data on how millions of real users actually interact with AI tools.
The author proposes creating a service similar to Google Trends to provide researchers with aggregated, near-real-time data on AI usage trends while preserving user privacy.
The text notes that while some companies like OpenAI and Anthropic publish usage dashboards, they often frame data in ways that limit external scrutiny of societal risks.
items.summary: Oliver Marsh argues that auditing AI chatbots is insufficient for understanding societal risks because it does not reflect how millions of people actually use these tools. He proposes a 'Google Trends for AI' service that would provide researchers with aggregated, near-real-time data on usage trends while preserving privacy. Marsh notes that while companies like OpenAI and Anthropic publish usage dashboards, they often frame data to limit external scrutiny. He suggests that transparency laws or voluntary codes of practice could mandate such services, noting that refusing to provide them would raise questions about corporate commitments to risk mitigation.
items.title: Author Calls for Google Trends Model for AI Usage Data

key_points: OpenAI will share its AI cyber defence system Daybreak for free with the Ukrainian government to protect civilian infrastructure from cyber-attacks.
Experts note that while such initiatives strengthen Ukraine's cyber defence, the technology itself poses dual-use risks for both attackers and defenders.
items.summary: OpenAI announced it will provide its AI cyber defence system, Daybreak, to Ukraine for free to help protect civilian infrastructure like hospitals and power plants. According to CERT-UA, Ukraine recorded nearly 6,000 attacks in 2025. While experts welcome the support as a force multiplier, analysts note that advanced AI models can be used for both defence and attack, highlighting the dual-use nature of the technology.
items.title: OpenAI Provides Free AI Cyber Defence Tools to Ukraine

key_points: StarHub and Keppel confirmed ongoing discussions regarding a potential deal involving M1, marking the latest consolidation effort in Singapore's telecommunications sector.
The talks follow the collapse of a previous acquisition attempt by Simba due to regulatory issues concerning unauthorized spectrum usage.
Analysts suggest such consolidation is necessary to improve industry returns amidst intense price competition and weakening earnings for incumbent operators.
items.summary: StarHub and Keppel have confirmed they are in talks over a potential deal involving M1, signaling further consolidation in Singapore's telecommunications sector. This discussion follows the collapse of a $1.4 billion acquisition attempt by Simba in May 2026, which fell through after the Infocomm Media Development Authority suspended its assessment due to Simba's unauthorized spectrum usage. Analysts note that operating four mobile operators yields weak returns, suggesting consolidation is needed to improve revenue. Temasek, a controlling shareholder of both StarHub and Keppel, holds significant interests in the companies involved. Meanwhile, StarHub and M1 have been implementing cost-saving initiatives to prepare for potential integration.
items.title: StarHub and Keppel Confirm Talks for Potential M1 Deal

key_points: The article argues that current AI risk discussions focus too much on technical model failures rather than the immediate impacts on people and their rights.
Authors cite incidents involving Anthropic and OpenAI as examples where the conversation centered on model capabilities instead of broader governance and human consequences.
items.summary: Jenny Domino and Jen Weedon argue that mainstream AI risk discourse prioritizes technical model failures over the immediate impacts on people and their rights. Citing incidents involving Anthropic and OpenAI, the authors note that discussions often focus on model capabilities rather than broader governance issues or human consequences. They propose adopting a human rights lens to better identify affected communities, allocate accountability to human actors like states and companies, and ensure effective remedies for harms caused by AI systems. This approach would shift focus from abstract technical risks to specific rights implications, such as freedom of expression and access to information.
items.title: Authors Argue for Human Rights Focus in AI Risk Discourse

key_points: McDonald's is committing $10.8 billion to help franchisees improve food quality, service, and operational efficiency through 2036.
The company faces slowing US sales and competition, prompting a strategy to modernize restaurants and adjust growth targets.
items.summary: McDonald's has announced a $10.8 billion investment to assist franchisees in improving food quality, service, and operational efficiency through 2036. The initiative, named 'Next,' aims to modernize restaurants and address challenges such as slowing US business and fierce competition from emerging brands. Consequently, the company is adjusting its growth targets and simplifying its marketing strategy to better compete in the market.
items.title: McDonald's Announces $10.8 Billion Investment Plan

key_points: The author observes widespread AI adoption among train passengers and notes that half of adults in a US study reported using AI chatbots.
While AI offers speed and cost savings, it risks deskilling professionals and undermining self-correction through sycophantic behavior.
The author concludes that the relationship with AI is a partnership requiring constant vigilance to prevent the decay of human thinking and skills.
items.summary: Setareh Seyedghorban, an academic researcher, describes her complex relationship with AI tools as seductive yet demanding vigilance. Observing widespread adoption on trains and citing a US study where half of adults use chatbots, she notes the benefits of speed and cost reduction. However, she highlights risks such as 'sycophancy' undermining self-correction and 'deskilling' in medical contexts. While AI levels the playing field for non-native speakers, she warns that human judgment remains essential. She concludes that the future lies not in divorce or honeymoon phases, but in a real partnership where humans maintain control over their thinking and skills.
items.title: Academic Reflects on Complex and Vigilant Relationship with AI Tools

key_points: InfraTrust reported that attackers are increasingly targeting network management systems, exploiting critical vulnerabilities before or shortly after vendor disclosure.
The September report tracked 158 new advisories across 17 vendors, covering 1,699 vulnerabilities, with 42 rated critical and 71 exploitable remotely.
Major vendors like Cisco and SonicWall have confirmed active exploitation of specific flaws, prompting CISA to add them to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
items.summary: InfraTrust's September report highlights a surge in attacks targeting network management systems used to control enterprise infrastructure. Between August 25 and September 17, the organization tracked 158 new security advisories across 17 vendors, covering 1,699 vulnerabilities. Of these, 42 were rated critical, with 71 capable of remote exploitation without authentication. Major vendors, including Cisco and SonicWall, confirmed active exploitation of specific flaws, leading CISA to add them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The report emphasizes that attackers are focusing on administrative software, treating these platforms as high-value targets.
items.title: InfraTrust Report Warns of Rising Attacks on Network Management Systems

key_points: The move follows microdramas surpassing 6.5 billion views on the platform in the first half of the year, with industry revenue estimated at $14 billion in 2026.
items.summary: YouTube announced a new feature enabling creators to organize vertical clips into microdrama-style series, aiming to capitalize on the genre's rapid growth. Executives stated they are excited about the rise of episodic content, noting that microdramas have already surpassed 6.5 billion views on the platform in the first half of the year. The microdrama industry is estimated to generate $14 billion in revenue in 2026.
items.title: YouTube Launches Microdrama Series Feature Amid Industry Boom

key_points: StrictlyVC at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will host investors and experts to discuss the changing landscape of venture capital driven by AI and startup scaling.
The event features sessions on new IPO requirements, the rising influence of family offices, and current limited partner expectations in the market.
items.summary: StrictlyVC at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco will convene investors and experts to examine the evolving venture capital landscape. Driven by AI and rapid startup scaling, the event offers sessions on new IPO rules, the growing role of family offices, and current limited partner expectations. Registration for the Investor Pass is required by September 25 to secure a $200 discount.
items.title: StrictlyVC Event Explores Shifting Venture Capital Rules at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026

key_points: YouTube announced new AI features for the Studio app to help creators analyze videos and grow audiences.
Updates include expanding Ask Studio to mobile, generating dynamic thumbnails, and automatically monitoring thumbnail performance.
items.summary: At its Made on YouTube event, the platform announced new AI tools within the Studio app designed to assist creators in analyzing content and expanding their reach. Key updates include expanding the Ask Studio feature to mobile devices and introducing AI capabilities for generating dynamic thumbnails and feedback on video drafts. Additionally, YouTube plans to automatically monitor thumbnail performance and update analytics to explain video engagement beyond raw numbers.
items.title: YouTube Announces New AI Tools for Creators in Studio App

key_points: Tesla's racism trial in California opened with allegations that company lawyers contacted witnesses to influence their testimony.
A senior Tesla attorney allegedly misled a former employee into believing he was working for the state during a call.
items.summary: Tesla's racism trial in California opened on Monday with a difficult start for the company's legal team. The California Civil Rights Department (CRD) sued Tesla on behalf of over 6,000 Black workers at its Fremont factory. During the trial, a senior Tesla attorney, Timothy Kim, allegedly contacted a former employee, Ryan Edwards, and misled him into thinking he was working for the state. Edwards testified that Kim steered him toward saying Tesla was a good place to work and offered to represent him. Additionally, the CRD reported that four other witnesses have gone silent, possibly due to contact by Tesla's legal team. Tesla's lawyer argued that the N-word is a term of endearment in the Black community, citing rap lyrics. The trial is expected to run through October, with damages uncapped. Judge Peter Borkon will decide the case.
items.title: Tesla Lawyers Face Accusations of Witness Tampering in Racism Trial

key_points: The facility, built in 12 months with 900 workers, covers 400 hectares and includes environmental measures like planting 38,000 trees.
items.summary: UK-based company Nadara has completed the 227 MW Big Fish agrivoltaic project in Sicily, which it describes as Italy's largest of its kind. Supported by a 156 MW power purchase agreement with Amazon, the facility was constructed in 12 months involving over 900 workers. Spanning 400 hectares across three municipalities, the project dedicates half the area to agriculture while implementing environmental measures such as planting 38,000 trees and restoring 2.5 km of waterways. Local municipalities are expected to receive at least €17.25 million over the project's life.
items.title: Nadara and Amazon Complete Italy's Largest Agrivoltaic Facility

key_points: Copper prices extended a winning streak, closing near record highs as Chinese buyers restocked ahead of holidays and warehouse inventories in Shanghai and London continued to drain.
Shanghai copper cathode stocks fell to 43,900 tons, the lowest since 2023, while global mined output could fall this year for the first time since 2017 due to outages at major mines.
items.summary: Copper prices extended a winning streak, closing near record highs as Chinese buyers restocked ahead of holidays and warehouse inventories in Shanghai and London continued to drain. Shanghai copper cathode stocks fell to 43,900 tons, the lowest since 2023, while global mined output could fall this year for the first time since 2017 due to outages at major mines. Analysts warn the rally may be inflated, with some predicting a potential market correction of 20% to 30% if Chinese producers begin selling as prices climb further.
items.title: Copper Prices Rise as Chinese Stockpiles Hit Three-Year Low Amid Supply Concerns

key_points: U.S. crude oil inventories increased by 3 million barrels to 426.4 million, which is 2% above the five-year average, according to new data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration.
items.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration reported that crude oil inventories in the United States increased by 3 million barrels during the week ending September 18, bringing commercial stockpiles to 426.4 million barrels, which is 2% above the five-year average. Conversely, distillate inventories decreased by 400,000 barrels and are now 12% below the five-year average. Total products supplied averaged 20.6 million barrels per day over the last four weeks, up 0.5% compared to the same period last year.
items.title: U.S. Crude Oil Inventories Rise While Distillate Stocks Fall

key_points: Poland's Energy Regulatory Office will conduct seven price-only auctions between November 2 and 10 to allocate support for over 76 TWh of new renewable energy.
The auctions prioritize photovoltaic and onshore wind projects, reserving 64.5 TWh for these technologies, with the largest portion designated for installations exceeding 1 MW.
items.summary: Poland's Energy Regulatory Office (URE) announced on September 22 that it will run seven price-only auctions from November 2 to November 10 for new renewable energy installations. The auctions aim to allocate support for more than 76 TWh of electricity, valued at nearly PLN 25 billion. A significant portion, 64.5 TWh, is reserved for photovoltaic and onshore wind projects, with 53.25 TWh specifically set aside for installations larger than 1 MW competing in a final auction on November 10. Bids will be assessed solely on price, adhering to a 2022 government regulation that caps annual auction volumes through 2027.
items.title: Poland Announces Large-Scale Renewable Energy Auctions for November

key_points: Nissan is reviving the Pixo nameplate to launch an affordable all-electric city cruiser priced under $25,000, targeting Europe's growing A-segment market.
items.summary: Nissan is reviving the Pixo nameplate to launch an affordable all-electric city cruiser priced under $25,000, targeting Europe's growing A-segment market. Developed through a partnership with Renault, the vehicle features a 27.5 kWh battery offering up to 259 km of range and will be produced at Renault's plant in Slovenia. Nissan stated the car is designed for drivers seeking accessible electric city mobility with modern connectivity.
items.title: Nissan Revives Pixo Name for Affordable European Electric City Car

key_points: Uber stock volatility follows reports that Tesla's autonomous Cybercabs could undercut its market share and pricing.
Recent filings show Uber executives bought shares while a corporate officer sold, alongside management projecting robotaxi expansion to 15 cities by year-end.
items.summary: Uber Technologies Inc. faces market scrutiny after videos of Tesla Cybercabs suggest a threat to its ride-hailing dominance. While bears warn that Tesla's direct customer access and lower prices could erode Uber's margins, the company's management highlights its established network and partnerships with multiple autonomous vehicle providers. Recent insider activity shows mixed signals, with CEO Dara Khosrowshahi and COO Andrew Macdonald purchasing shares, while Chief Corporate Officer Jill Hazelbaker sold a portion of her holdings. Management projects robotaxi services to 15 cities by year-end, though valuation metrics remain below Uber's historical average.
items.title: Uber Shares Face Scrutiny Amid Tesla Robotaxi Competition and Insider Trading

key_points: Rallies Arena provided Claude AI with a $100,000 portfolio to beat the S&P 500, resulting in EMCOR Group and NVIDIA as top holdings.
EMCOR Group leads the portfolio at 17.7%, driven by its role in building data center infrastructure required for high-power AI campuses.
items.summary: Rallies Arena tasked Claude AI with managing a $100,000 portfolio to outperform the S&P 500. The model selected EMCOR Group and NVIDIA as its largest positions. EMCOR, a construction firm specializing in data center infrastructure, holds 17.7% of the portfolio. Analysts note EMCOR benefits from the power and cooling needs of new AI campuses, which require significantly more capacity than older facilities. Goldman Sachs forecasts global AI investment exceeding $1 trillion in 2026.
items.title: Claude AI September Portfolio Highlights EMCOR and NVIDIA

key_points: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated there is a fair case for the rupee to stabilize or appreciate despite recent pressures.
India's economy has emerged structurally stronger from recent shocks, supported by resilient growth and a declining current account deficit.
items.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta argued at the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave that the rupee has a fair case to stabilize or appreciate. She noted India has emerged structurally stronger from recent shocks, with a resilient growth equilibrium of 7% plus. Although the rupee hit a record low of 96.96 against the US dollar in May, it closed at 95.74. Gupta highlighted that despite huge inflows of $133 billion via FCNR deposits, the market dynamics do not appear well-founded for depreciation. She expects the current account deficit to shrink further, underpinned by growing success in merchandise exports and a resilient growth equilibrium.
items.title: RBI Deputy Governor Sees Case for Rupee Appreciation Amid Economic Resilience

key_points: Amazon introduced a new agentic AI service for third-party sellers to automate listing and inventory management tasks.
The optional service is free and allows sellers to control data sharing while connecting to existing AI tools.
items.summary: Amazon introduced a new agentic artificial intelligence service for third-party sellers on its main e-commerce site to expand automation features for listing and inventory management. Known as 'workflows,' the service runs continuously to handle seller prompts such as rating alerts and pricing monitoring. The optional service is free, and sellers can decide how much personal data they share with Amazon. Amazon's Mary Beth Westmoreland, vice president of worldwide selling experience, confirmed these details.
items.title: Amazon Launches Agentic AI Service for Third-Party Sellers

key_points: Anthropic and OpenAI leaders will brief the UN Security Council today regarding AI development slowdowns.
Global perspectives on AI vary, with the Global South showing more optimism than the West.
items.summary: The heads of Anthropic and OpenAI are set to brief the UN Security Council today, highlighting their calls for a slowdown in AI development amidst superpower competition. While Washington and Beijing are unlikely to reach a wide-ranging pact, the UK plans to focus its G20 presidency on AI safety. Global perspectives diverge, with the Global South appearing more optimistic about AI than the West.
items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI Leaders to Brief UN Security Council on AI

key_points: Josh Parker, Nvidia's head of sustainability, stated that anti-AI sentiment is driven by a fundamental human fear of the unknown.
Parker emphasized that responsible AI deployment connects safety and sustainability, noting that different themes receive varying attention over time.
items.summary: Josh Parker, Nvidia's head of sustainability, addressed recent anti-AI sentiment at Semafor's The Next 3 Billion event. He attributed the backlash to a fundamental human fear of the unknown and highlighted the need for transparency regarding data center sustainability results. Parker noted that prioritizing safety and sustainability is not inconsistent, as responsible AI deployment remains a common thread despite shifting public attention.
items.title: Nvidia Exec Attributes AI Backlash to Fear of the Unknown

key_points: The company plans to expand its YouTube Shopping affiliate program to 35 countries by year-end, building on a base of over 1.3 million enrolled creators.
items.summary: On September 23, Alphabet-owned YouTube unveiled a suite of artificial intelligence tools, shopping updates, and personalized viewer features at its annual Made on YouTube event in New York City. The new creator tools include additions to YouTube Studio for feedback on video drafts, channel-matched thumbnails, and testing up to three video cuts. A Gemini-powered assistant in Shorts and YouTube Create will help edit clips, trim pauses, and sync music. The platform is also testing opt-in AI comment moderation that adapts to creators' preferences and will combine voice and facial detection in its likeness-protection tools.
items.title: YouTube Unveils AI Tools and Shopping Features at Annual Event

key_points: A White House spokesperson stated that Trump's portfolio is independently managed by third parties with no ability to direct investments or conflicts of interest.
items.summary: US President Donald Trump disclosed millions of dollars in stock market trades made during July, involving companies such as Microsoft, Nvidia, Palantir, SpaceX, and Tesla. Official documents show sales of Microsoft stock worth between $6.5m and $31m, alongside purchases of other tech shares across more than 1,000 trades. A White House spokesperson stated that Trump's portfolio is independently managed by third parties, asserting that neither Trump nor his family can direct investments or that conflicts of interest exist.
items.title: Trump Discloses Millions in Tech Stock Trades Amid Conflict Concerns

key_points: Ursula von der Leyen suggested Canada could become the EU's first associate member, a concept that lacks a legal definition or blueprint.
Experts note that creating such a status would require treaty reform, which member states are unlikely to contemplate.
While the proposal offers a potential counterweight to US trade threats, it remains a political hypothesis rather than a concrete reality.
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen recently proposed that Canada become the EU's first associate member, citing shared stances on global issues. However, the article clarifies that 'associate membership' is not a defined status in EU treaties and lacks a blueprint. While Canada seeks closer ties to diversify relations away from US trade threats, experts suggest a realistic partnership would resemble the EU-Swiss relationship rather than full integration. The proposal remains a political hypothesis, reflecting a desire for strategic alignment without formal membership.
items.title: EU and Canada explore vague associate membership amid global uncertainty

key_points: The European Commission plans to coordinate with Washington to minimize disruption from new US tariffs on Russian energy.
The EU faces potential LNG supply squeezes as it struggles to refill storage levels to 80% by November amid competition from Asian bidders.
European politicians urge companies like Fayard to stop servicing Russian LNG vessels to maintain pressure on Moscow.
items.summary: The European Commission stated it will collaborate with Washington to mitigate disruption from US tariffs on Russian energy. The EU faces potential liquefied natural gas supply squeezes as it struggles to refill storage levels to at least 80% by November, according to Global Energy Flow. While the Lindsey Graham Sanctions Act allows tariffs up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil or gas, its application to the EU remains uncertain. EU officials hope the law does not create new commercial barriers. Meanwhile, European politicians criticized companies like Fayard for servicing Russian LNG vessels, arguing such actions sustain Russia's war effort.
items.title: EU and US officials discuss LNG risks from Trump tariffs

key_points: Hainan Province is expanding its low-carbon economy through a natural gas network that has transmitted over 35 billion cubic meters of gas, replacing millions of tonnes of coal and reducing emissions.
The province plans to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, with clean energy projected to account for 87.2% of power capacity by the end of 2025.
items.summary: Hainan Province is intensifying efforts to build a low-carbon economy, highlighted by its first island-loop natural gas pipeline network surpassing 35 billion cubic meters in cumulative transmission. According to PipeChina, this network has replaced an estimated 46.6 million tonnes of coal, significantly reducing dust and carbon dioxide emissions. Beyond energy supply, the island is advancing a ban on new fuel-powered vehicles by 2030 and aims for clean energy to comprise 87.2% of power capacity by the end of 2025. Long-term targets include peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality by 2060.
items.title: Hainan Province Advances Low-Carbon Economy with Pipeline and Clean Energy Goals

key_points: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for a multilateral AI Risk Management Framework to address the concentration and speed of AI development.
Guterres emphasized that governments must assume responsibility for protecting people, ensuring transparency, and preventing the use of AI in life-and-death decisions.
items.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres addressed the 81st United Nations General Assembly, calling for steps to manage artificial intelligence risks. He argued that power now stems from data and algorithms, which advance faster than our ability to understand them. Guterres urged governments to assume responsibility, establish transparency, and cooperate on testing and safeguards. He highlighted the need for a multilateral AI Risk Management Framework and stated that killer robots must have no place in the future.
items.title: UN Chief Urges Global Coordination to Manage AI Risks

key_points: President Donald Trump announced a rebranding of artificial intelligence to 'super intelligence' during his UN General Assembly address.
He argued the new term better reflects the technology's capabilities and opposed broad international regulation to maintain U.S. leadership.
items.summary: During his address to the UN General Assembly, President Donald Trump promoted a new designation for artificial intelligence, suggesting the government refer to it as 'super intelligence' or SI. He stated that the existing term understates the technology's capabilities. Additionally, Trump rejected calls for broad international regulation, arguing the United States should focus on maintaining its technological lead while avoiding rules that could slow development. His remarks followed announcements regarding an 'AI Force' and plans for an AI 'czar.'
items.title: Trump Renames AI to Super Intelligence at UN Address

key_points: Beijing seeks greater representation for developing nations, though the practical implications remain unexplained.
items.summary: China's Global Governance Initiative is built on the principle that every country deserves a voice in shaping the rules affecting its future. Beijing aims to increase representation for developing nations, but the article notes that the practical meaning of this goal is yet to be defined. CGTN's Ediz Tiyansan reports on this stance from the United Nations in New York City.
items.title: China Advocates Equal Voice for Nations at UN

key_points: Ethiopia's government and Tigrayan authorities accuse each other of launching offensives, escalating fears of renewed conflict in the region.
Reports indicate drone strikes in Tigray and Alamata, with local authorities claiming civilian casualties and federal forces targeting schools.
items.summary: Ethiopia's government and Tigrayan authorities are accusing each other of launching offensives, raising fears of a return to full-scale conflict. Getachew Reda stated Tigrayan fighters took control of airports and launched attacks in neighboring regions, while Tigrayan authorities claimed they were forced into a defensive war. Reports of drone strikes in Tigray and Alamata have resulted in civilian casualties, with local officials alleging federal forces targeted schools. The US State Department condemned a separate strike on a food aid convoy. Both sides face criticism for delays in implementing the Pretoria Agreement that ended the 2022 war.
items.title: Ethiopia and Tigray Accuse Each Other of Launching Offensives

key_points: US shares dropped on Wednesday as benchmark 10-year Treasury yields reached their highest level since 2007.
Strong US business activity data, with a PMI Output Index of 58.4, fueled expectations for further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
items.summary: US stocks fell on Wednesday as benchmark 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2007. This move followed data showing US business activity surged to a five-year high, driven by a rise in new orders. S&P Global reported its flash US Composite PMI Output Index increased to 58.4, the highest since July 2021. The strong economic data led traders to price in a higher likelihood of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, pushing yields to multi-year highs and causing equity markets to decline.
items.title: US Stocks Fall as Treasury Yields Hit Multi-Year Highs Amid Strong Economic Data

key_points: Six people were arrested after anti-migrant protesters gathered at a marina in Hampshire under the mistaken belief that a small boat carrying asylum seekers was due to arrive.
The protesters, heeding calls from far-right campaigner Daniel Thomas, aimed to disrupt disembarkation, but the Border Force vessels landed in Dover instead.
items.summary: Six people were arrested after anti-migrant protesters gathered at a marina in Hampshire, mistakenly believing a small boat carrying asylum seekers was due to arrive. Heeding calls from far-right campaigner Daniel Thomas, hundreds of protesters aimed to disrupt disembarkation, but the Border Force vessels landed in Dover instead. Police are conducting inquiries into Thomas for slashing an inflatable dinghy while a rescue worker was onboard. Two men and four women were arrested for aggravated trespass and assaulting an emergency worker. The Home Office plans to use public order powers to stop harassment of government staff.
items.title: Six Arrested After Anti-Migrant Protest at Hampshire Marina

key_points: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran will not surrender in the war with the United States but believes in diplomacy to end the conflict.
items.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the United Nations General Assembly on September 23, 2026, declaring that Iran will not surrender in its war with the United States but remains committed to diplomacy. During his rare wartime speech, Pezeshkian displayed images of the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and over 150 school children killed in early attacks. He asserted that the United States and Israel attacked Iran, while the U.S. delegation walked out at the start of the address. The Strait of Hormuz remains a focal point of tension between the nations.
items.title: Iranian President Rejects Surrender to U.S. While Calling for Diplomacy

key_points: Blind and visually impaired gamers are creating custom solutions like NFC tags and braille to play video and board games as industry giants release adapted controllers.
Microsoft and Sony have launched specialized controllers, while organizations like ONCE and the Accessible Games Initiative promote inclusive design standards.
Advocates note that while progress is being made, true accessibility requires early integration into game design rather than retroactive modifications.
items.summary: Gamers with visual or motor impairments are increasingly creating their own ways to keep playing as industry giants Microsoft, Sony and ONCE roll out adapted controllers alongside new video and board games. Blind player Cristian M. Amores uses NFC tags to read Magic: The Gathering cards, a solution he adopted after braille and QR codes proved impractical. Similarly, a Reddit group adapted a Commander deck using NFC tags to avoid the social isolation of relying on others to read cards aloud. In Spain, Proyecto Glirp advises publishers on accessibility, noting that inclusive design is often added too late. Meanwhile, Microsoft and Sony have released specialized controllers, and the Accessible Games Initiative aims to standardize accessibility features across the industry.
items.title: Gamers with impairments adapt games as industry adds tools

key_points: US President Donald Trump rejected international control efforts, emphasizing competition and rapid development, while other leaders called for common rules and safeguards.
Leaders like UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged for human control, international legal frameworks, and shared responsibility in managing AI risks.
items.summary: Artificial intelligence emerged as a major theme at the opening of the UN General Assembly, with world leaders warning about risks ranging from autonomous weapons to job disruption. However, little consensus exists on next steps. US President Donald Trump rejected international control efforts, emphasizing competition and rapid development, while leaders like UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan called for common rules and safeguards. Guterres warned that humanity is increasingly transferring power to machines, insisting life-and-death decisions must remain under human control. Other leaders, including British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron, highlighted the need for transparency, oversight, and international cooperation to prevent dominance by a few powers or companies. The debate underscores the tension between technological advancement and the establishment of global governance frameworks.
items.title: World Leaders Debate AI Governance at UN General Assembly

key_points: David Ellison, founder of Skydance, acquired Paramount and Warner Bros to build a massive entertainment empire in under two years.
The deal faced antitrust challenges from 12 Democratic attorneys general, which Ellison resolved by threatening to move studios to Nashville before reaffirming a Los Angeles headquarters.
Ellison, backed by his father Larry Ellison, leveraged $350 million in initial funding and strategic acquisitions to control major film catalogs and streaming platforms.
items.summary: David Ellison, a 43-year-old entrepreneur backed by his father Larry Ellison, has rapidly built a dominant position in Hollywood by acquiring Paramount and Warner Bros. Through Skydance, Ellison secured a vast film catalog and streaming platforms, consolidating two industry giants. The $110 billion merger faced opposition from 12 Democratic attorneys general alleging antitrust violations. Ellison countered by threatening to relocate studios to Nashville before confirming the merged company would remain in Los Angeles. The deal, approved after a payment to the White House, marks a significant shift in the industry's power structure.
items.title: David Ellison Consolidates Hollywood Empire Amid Antitrust Scrutiny

key_points: The funds will establish a new engineering school in Eugene, adding to the Knights' existing $2bn total giving to the university.
items.summary: Nike cofounder Phil Knight and his wife, Penny, donated $1bn to the University of Oregon, a gift believed to be the largest known donation to a flagship university. The funds will establish a new engineering school in Eugene. This donation brings the Knights' known total giving to the university to more than $2bn. The university president, Karl Scholz, called it a tremendous endorsement of higher education.
items.title: Nike Cofounder Phil Knight Makes Historic $1bn Donation to University of Oregon

key_points: Turkish First Lady Emine Erdogan concluded a busy agenda in New York covering issues concerning humanity and future-shaping topics during the 81st UN General Assembly.
items.summary: Turkish First Lady Emine Erdogan concluded a busy agenda in New York covering issues concerning humanity and future-shaping topics during the 81st UN General Assembly. She shared a video highlighting her participation in events, including President Erdogan's address and the International Energy Agency High-Level Energy Transition Dialogue. Erdogan stated that the agenda covered topics that will shape the future of the world.
items.title: Turkish First Lady Emine Erdogan Discusses Global Issues in New York

key_points: The National Elections Commission called on politicians and parties to ensure a peaceful electoral process.
President Salva Kiir dissolved the transitional government to clear the way for the December 22 election.
items.summary: South Sudan's National Elections Commission chairperson Gabriel Bol Deng Majok urged politicians and parties to convert political ideas into ballots rather than bullets. The commission emphasized its role in leveling the playing field with rules and regulations. President Salva Kiir dissolved the transitional government on Tuesday, paving the way for the general election scheduled for December 22. Preparations are underway for the first polls since independence in 2011.
items.title: South Sudan Election Commission Urges Politicians for Peaceful Polls

key_points: The conviction marks a significant milestone, though challenges remain regarding justice and funding for ongoing efforts in the region.
items.summary: Judges at the International Criminal Court convicted former rebel commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani of crimes against humanity for abusing and torturing prisoners at a detention facility in the Central African Republic. Witnesses described inhumane conditions, including cramped cells and confinement under floorboards. While the verdict offers recognition to victims, experts warn that closing the ICC investigation and potential funding cuts to local courts threaten future accountability in the region.
items.title: ICC Convicts CAR Rebel Commander for Crimes Against Humanity

key_points: Indian officials allege LG and Samsung wrongly claimed a 5% tariff on imported OLED glass screens, arguing a 15% duty should apply.
Industry groups are lobbying for OLED parts to receive the same low-duty benefits as LCD and LED components to maintain competitiveness.
Samsung is reviewing the matter and cooperating with authorities, while LG has submitted responses and a voluntary deposit to cover potential extra duties.
items.summary: Indian officials have launched an investigation into LG Electronics and Samsung, alleging the companies incorrectly claimed a 5% concessional tariff on imported OLED glass screens. Authorities believe a 15% duty should apply, as OLED parts are not covered under the lower rate reserved for older LCD and LED technology. While Samsung states it is reviewing the matter and cooperating fully, LG has submitted responses and a voluntary deposit. Industry groups are lobbying for policy changes to ensure OLED manufacturers receive parity with legacy technologies.
items.title: India Investigates LG and Samsung Over OLED Tariff Claims

key_points: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated there is a fair case for the Indian Rupee to stabilize or appreciate following recent capital flow measures.
She noted that India's cumulative depreciation of 13.1% since March 2025 is likely a temporary phenomenon due to oil and gold price shocks.
items.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated there is a fair case for the Indian Rupee to stabilize or appreciate following recent capital flow measures announced in June 2026. She noted that India's cumulative depreciation of 13.1% since March 31, 2025, is likely a temporary phenomenon driven by oil and gold price shocks. Gupta highlighted that India's economy is growing at 7-8% in real terms and expects the current account deficit to shrink further, supported by resilient net services exports and remittances.
items.title: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta suggests Rupee may appreciate

key_points: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has launched penal actions against five major e-commerce platforms for regulatory non-compliances.
Violations include misleading claims, misbranding, and the sale of prohibited food items like Datura fruits and specific dairy products.
items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) announced on Wednesday that it has initiated penal action against five leading e-commerce platforms: Amazon, Swiggy Instamart, BigBasket, Flipkart India, and Zepto. The regulator cited various non-compliances, including misleading claims, misbranding, and the sale of prohibited or poisonous food articles. Specific instances involved misleading claims regarding 'Happilo Premium Date Bites' and non-compliant dairy products from Milky Mist. Additionally, platforms were found non-compliant with provisions relating to the sale of Datura fruits and seeds. FSSAI officials stated that email queries sent to these platforms elicited no immediate response.
items.title: FSSAI Initiates Penal Action Against Major E-commerce Platforms for Food Safety Violations

key_points: The company states this validates its ability to help customers accelerate innovation and modernize application delivery through AI-driven engineering practices.
items.summary: IFI Techsolutions Limited announced it has achieved the Agentic DevOps specialization with Microsoft Azure and GitHub. The achievement, awarded after a rigorous third-party audit, validates the company's technical expertise and delivery excellence. David Wright, Chief Revenue Officer, stated the specialization confirms their ability to help customers accelerate innovation and create measurable business value through AI-powered engineering practices.
items.title: IFI Techsolutions Achieves Agentic DevOps Specialization with Microsoft and GitHub

key_points: The regulator cited issues such as misbranding, misleading claims, and the sale of prohibited food articles but did not specify which violations applied to each platform.
items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) announced on Wednesday that it has initiated penal action against five e-commerce platforms: Amazon, Swiggy Instamart, BigBasket, Flipkart India, and Zepto. The regulator described the move as a crackdown on regulatory non-compliances, citing issues such as misbranding, misleading claims, and the sale or display of prohibited or poisonous food articles. However, FSSAI did not specify which alleged violations applied to each platform, nor did it identify the specific products involved or the penalties being pursued.
items.title: FSSAI Initiates Penal Action Against Five E-Commerce Platforms Over Alleged Food Safety Violations

key_points: Youth Congress members protested outside IIT Bombay demanding justice for student Sahil Wakode, who died after the institute alleged he cheated using ChatGPT.
Wakode's family seeks arrests of those named in the case and a fair investigation, while alleging caste-based harassment contributed to his death.
items.summary: Youth Congress members protested outside IIT Bombay on Wednesday, demanding justice for student Sahil Wakode following his death. The demonstration targeted the institute's statement alleging Wakode cheated using ChatGPT during an exam before committing suicide. Wakode's advocate, Nikhil Kamble, stated the family seeks arrests of those named in the case to progress the investigation. Additionally, the family alleges their son faced caste-based harassment, though details remain under investigation by the Mumbai Crime Branch.
items.title: Youth Congress Protests IIT Bombay Over ChatGPT Cheating Claim Following Student Death

key_points: British sociologist Michael Young coined 'meritocracy' in 1958 as a warning against new elites convinced their privilege was earned.
Vijaye Raji and Rahul Patil lead technical operations at OpenAI and Anthropic respectively, having reached top roles without IIT degrees despite the credential's reverence in India.
items.summary: British sociologist Michael Young coined the term 'meritocracy' in 1958 as a warning against a new elite convinced their privilege was earned. TIME magazine's list of tech leaders includes Indian-origin executives like Vijaye Raji of OpenAI and Rahul Patil of Anthropic. Neither studied at an Indian Institute of Technology, a credential treated with reverence in India. Raji holds a degree from Pondicherry Engineering College and Patil from PESIT, both achieving top technical roles without the specific degree their home country often values above all.
items.title: Indian-Origin CTOs Lead Top AI Firms Without IIT Degrees

key_points: The death toll from a fire at the Special Neonatal Care Unit in Adilabad has risen to five after two more infants succumbed on Tuesday night.
items.summary: The death toll from a fire at the Special Neonatal Care Unit of Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences in Adilabad has risen to five. Two premature infants died on Tuesday night, September 22, 2026, following an incident that began on September 21 when an air conditioner burst into flames. The Telangana government announced an ex gratia of ₹5 lakh to the families of the deceased children. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has ordered an inquiry into the incident.
items.title: Death toll rises to five after fire at Adilabad SNCU

key_points: An 8.5-km stretch along the JNTU-Miyapur-Raidurg Metro corridor will undergo a mobility assessment to address footpath gaps, unsafe crossings, and traffic bottlenecks.
The study, chaired by Special Chief Secretary Jayesh Ranjan, will evaluate pedestrian access, feeder services, and school-related traffic congestion to improve last-mile connectivity.
items.summary: The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation announced an end-to-end mobility assessment for an 8.5-km stretch of the JNTU-Miyapur-Raidurg Metro corridor. The study, chaired by Special Chief Secretary Jayesh Ranjan, aims to address missing footpaths, unsafe pedestrian crossings, and traffic bottlenecks. Officials will evaluate pedestrian movement, feeder services, and school-related traffic congestion. The assessment highlights a growing dependence on private transport, noting a significant increase in daily trips in Hyderabad between 2011 and 2024.
items.title: Hyderabad to assess 8.5-km Metro corridor mobility and connectivity

key_points: Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Dutta rejected the notion that judges appoint judges, stating the judiciary plays a secondary role to the government in appointments.
He argued that selective executive implementation undermines collegium sanctity but affirmed the system remains the most viable option for safeguarding judicial independence under Article 50.
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Dutta defended the collegium system, rejecting the 'myth' that judges appoint judges. He argued the judiciary plays a secondary role to the government, noting selective executive implementation undermines collegium sanctity. Despite opacity, he affirmed the system remains the most viable option for safeguarding independence under Article 50 of the Constitution, delivered in a split verdict with Justice Satish Chandra Sharma.
items.title: SC Justice Datta Defends Collegium System Against Government Criticism

key_points: Rubio confirmed the meeting on social media, highlighting the strengthening of US-India strategic partnership and coordination on regional priorities.
items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in New York to discuss the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act. Rubio confirmed the meeting on social media, stating they are building on the US-India strategic partnership and coordinating on key regional priorities and upcoming multilateral efforts. The discussion took place on Wednesday in the context of broader bilateral ties.
items.title: India's Jaishankar Discusses Russia Sanctions Act with US Secretary Rubio

key_points: Bitcoin traded near $86,500, having gained nearly 14% over the past week, driven by returning institutional demand.
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs drew roughly $999 million in net inflows on September 21, marking their strongest daily inflow since October 2025. Bitcoin traded near $86,500 after gaining almost 14% over the past week. Experts attribute the rally to the return of institutional demand and ETF flows rather than organic spot buying. The broader crypto market capitalization rose toward $2.93 trillion with 24-hour trading volume at approximately $110.73 billion.
items.title: Bitcoin ETF Inflows Hit 11-Month High as Price Holds Near $86,000

key_points: Ten midcap stocks surged between 50% and 105% over six months while the broader Nifty 50 index remained flat with just under 1% gain.
items.summary: While the Nifty 50 index gained just under 1% over the last six months, the Nifty Midcap 150 index delivered a 13% gain. Ten midcap stocks emerged as standout performers, soaring between 50% and 105% during the same period. The article examines foreign institutional investor and mutual fund holdings in these high-performing stocks as of the June 2026 quarter.
items.title: Ten Midcap Stocks Soared Over Six Months Amid Flat Nifty 50

key_points: Students and alumni of Lady Shri Ram College in Delhi protested against sexual violence and safety lapses, citing a lack of streetlights, non-functional police booths, and absent CCTV cameras around the campus back gate.

The demonstration highlighted recurring incidents of sexual harassment and the fear of stepping out after dark, urging authorities to ensure active police deployment and adequate lighting to safeguard women.
items.summary: Students and alumni of Delhi's Lady Shri Ram College, alongside local mothers and professionals, gathered to protest against sexual violence and safety lapses around the campus. Protesters highlighted recent rape incidents and demanded urgent institutional and governmental action. Speakers raised serious concerns regarding safety around the college's back gate and Amar Colony, noting the total absence of streetlights, non-functional pink police booths, and a lack of CCTV cameras. An alumna highlighted the persistent fear of stepping out after dark and the risks of harassment along daily transit routes.
items.title: LSR Students Protest Safety Lapses and Harassment Near Campus

key_points: LSR students and alumni protested sexual violence and safety issues like dark lanes and inactive police booths around Lady Shri Ram College in Delhi.
items.summary: Students and alumni of Lady Shri Ram College in Delhi protested against sexual violence and safety lapses, citing dark lanes, inactive pink police booths, and a lack of streetlights. Former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa questioned the procedural legality of actions taken by the Election Commission of India regarding modifications to Form 6 and the centralisation of the voter database, highlighting concerns over statutory powers and internal dissent.
items.title: LSR Students Protest Safety Lapses and Election Commission Scrutiny

key_points: The Special Court for POCSO Cases sentenced 63-year-old K. Muthaiah to 20 years in prison for sexually abusing an 11-year-old girl in 2021.
items.summary: The Special Court for POCSO Cases sentenced 63-year-old K. Muthaiah to 20 years in prison for sexually abusing an 11-year-old girl in 2021. The court imposed a fine of ₹1.02 lakh on the accused and directed the Tamil Nadu Government to pay ₹3 lakh compensation to the victim. The judgment was delivered by Magistrate Murugan on Tuesday.
items.title: Special Court Sentences 63-Year-Old Man to 20 Years for POCSO Offense

key_points: The Government Railway Police in Tiruchi seized over 1,220 kilograms of gutkha across three sub-divisions from January to August this year.
Virudhunagar recorded the maximum seizure of 471 kilograms, followed by Madurai with 209 kg and Tirunelveli with 119 kg.
items.summary: The Government Railway Police (GRP) in Tiruchi reported seizing over 1,220 kilograms of gutkha between January and August this year across its jurisdiction. Data indicates Virudhunagar led with 471 kilograms seized, followed by Madurai at 209 kg and Tirunelveli at 119 kg. Officials attribute these seizures to illegal transport via inter-state trains from northern and eastern states where the substance is legal, into Tamil Nadu where it is banned. Dedicated teams conduct random checks and coordinate with local police and the Food Safety Department to handle confiscated contraband.
items.title: Railway Police Seize Over 1,000 kg of Banned Tobacco in Tamil Nadu

key_points: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian accused the United States and Israel of terrorism and aggression during his address to the United Nations General Assembly.
Pezeshkian defended Iran's nuclear program as a pursuit of energy rather than weapons while rejecting characterizations of Iran as an aggressor.
The speech highlighted the Minab school attack and Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's assassination as evidence of Iranian victimhood and justified Iran's military response.
items.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the United Nations General Assembly on September 23, accusing the United States and Israel of terrorism and aggression. He rejected descriptions of Iran as a terrorist state, stating Iranians were victims of terrorism, specifically citing the Minab school attack where over 100 children and teachers died. Pezeshkian defended Iran's nuclear program as a pursuit of energy, not weapons, and asserted Tehran acted in self-defense. Despite strong criticism, he expressed openness to diplomacy without military pressure, noting ongoing indirect discussions between US and Iranian officials mediated in New York.
items.title: Iranian President Accuses US and Israel of Terrorism at UN

key_points: The Tamil Nadu crime branch raided properties owned by industrialist R Veeramani and the Gem Group of Companies in connection with a Pocso case.
Shanthi, a former employee, alleged in a video that Veeramani made sexual advances toward her when she was 13 years old.
Police recovered documents and digital evidence, while a senior officer noted that Veeramani sold properties in February 2026 to evade arrest.
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu central crime branch raided properties belonging to industrialist R Veeramani and the Gem Group of Companies on Wednesday. The raids followed the arrest of Veeramani and three others, including former employee Ganeshan, in a Pocso case. Shanthi, a former aide, released a video claiming Veeramani made sexual advances toward her when she was 13. Police recovered documents and digital evidence during the search. A senior officer stated that Veeramani sold two properties in February 2026 to help him evade arrest. The case was reopened after a special court refused to accept a police report. Former BJP chief K Annamalai demanded a Special Investigation Team, while Education Minister A Rajmohan confirmed the investigation is under close monitoring by the chief minister.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Police Raid R Veeramani Properties Over Pocso Allegations

key_points: Global wheat buyers are facing a difficult choice as delayed purchases leave them with dwindling stocks while shipments from Russia and Ukraine remain disrupted.
Major importers like Egypt and Indonesia are turning to alternative suppliers such as France, Australia, and Argentina, though these options come with significantly higher costs.
items.summary: Global wheat buyers are facing a difficult choice as delayed purchases leave them with dwindling stocks while shipments from Russia and Ukraine remain disrupted. Major importers like Egypt and Indonesia are turning to alternative suppliers such as France, Australia, and Argentina, though these options come with significantly higher costs. The disruption has pushed benchmark wheat futures to a three-and-a-half-year high, intensifying competition for cargoes as buyers scramble to replenish inventories before Southern Hemisphere harvests arrive.
items.title: Russia-Ukraine War Disrupts Wheat Supplies, Forcing Buyers to Seek Alternatives

key_points: The Jammu and Kashmir government reported screening approximately 21.8 lakh books and withdrawing 4,812 from college libraries since July to ensure they do not contain inappropriate content.
The government stated that 518 withdrawn books were banned, while over 1,750 were referred for further examination under criteria aimed at upholding constitutional values and national interest.
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir government informed the Assembly that it screened approximately 21.8 lakh books and withdrew 4,812 from state-run and private college libraries since July. The government stated that 518 of the withdrawn books were banned, while more than 1,750 were referred for further examination. This action follows a directive to identify material violating religious sentiments or harming national interest, aiming to uphold constitutional values and academic freedom in educational institutions.
items.title: J&K Government Screens College Books Over Content Concerns

key_points: Sindhu Gangadharan, Managing Director of SAP Labs India, stated that enterprises must move beyond AI experimentation to focus on solving real business problems and building domain expertise.
items.summary: Sindhu Gangadharan, Managing Director of SAP Labs India, stated that enterprises must move beyond AI experimentation to focus on solving real business problems and building domain expertise. Speaking at the India Advantage Summit 2026, she emphasized that AI is a leadership transformation requiring organizations to start with desired outcomes rather than searching for problems where technology can be applied. She noted that while AI reduces solution build time, understanding business challenges and having strong data foundations remain essential for scaling initiatives beyond proof-of-concepts.
items.title: SAP Labs India MD urges shift from AI pilots to solving real business problems

key_points: Singer Pat Boone has listed his Beverly Hills estate, owned for 66 years, for $22.95 million, a significant increase from the original 1960 purchase price of $159,000.
The 1.12-acre property, built in 1939, features seven or eight bathrooms and has hosted notable figures like Elvis Presley and Gregory Peck over the decades.
Boone, now 92, stated he does not need such a large home but still enjoys it, marking the end of a long family chapter at the property.
items.summary: Singer and actor Pat Boone has listed his Beverly Hills estate for $22.95 million, ending a 66-year ownership that began in 1960 when he and his late wife Shirley purchased it for $159,000. The 1.12-acre property at 904 North Beverly Drive, built in 1939, features a residence with six bedrooms and between seven and eight bathrooms, along with a guest house and pool. Boone, now 92, told Mansion Global that while he does not need a place this big, he still loves the home where he raised his daughters and entertained celebrities like Elvis Presley. The current listing highlights the estate's potential for preservation or redevelopment, reflecting the dramatic rise in Beverly Hills real estate values over the last century.
items.title: Pat Boone's Beverly Hills Estate Listed for $22.95 Million

key_points: India categorically rejected Organisation of Islamic Cooperation remarks on Jammu and Kashmir as unwarranted and factually incorrect.
items.summary: India categorically rejected Organisation of Islamic Cooperation remarks on Jammu and Kashmir as unwarranted and factually incorrect. The Ministry of External Affairs stated the OIC lacks authority on strictly internal Indian matters and called for Pakistan to be counseled instead of supported. The ministry added that the Union Territories are integral parts of India and that the OIC's endorsement of such narratives raises doubts on its credibility.
items.title: India Rejects OIC Remarks on Jammu and Kashmir as Unwarranted

key_points: The agreement allows expanded US military operations in Greenland while affirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination.
It strengthens NATO engagement in the Arctic and prohibits non-NATO military installations in Greenland.
items.summary: US President Donald Trump, along with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland, signed an agreement in New York to address security concerns regarding the Arctic island. The deal permits the US to expand its military presence and modernize facilities at Pituffik Space Base while establishing defense areas elsewhere. It reaffirms Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination, supports stronger NATO engagement, and prohibits non-NATO military installations. The accord requires parliamentary approval before entering into force and remains valid indefinitely, allowing Greenland to join NATO if it becomes independent.
items.title: US, Denmark, and Greenland Sign Arctic Security Agreement

key_points: These factors contribute to an estimated daily loss of about ₹530 crore for the sector, driven by West Asia conflict and global supply dynamics.
items.summary: Credit rating agency ICRA reports that Indian oil marketing companies (OMCs) are facing significant financial strain, with estimated under-recoveries of ₹8 per litre on petrol, ₹9 on diesel, and nearly ₹300 on LPG cylinders. These margins translate to a daily loss of about ₹530 crore. Prashant Vashisht of ICRA attributes the situation to West Asia conflicts disrupting supply routes and rising crude oil prices, alongside global LPG supply concentration in the U.S., Australia, and Saudi Arabia.
items.title: Indian OMCs Face Daily Losses Amid Global Oil Disruption
